A user who tried several voice agent testing platforms said Cekura has been "the best by a long shot."
A user with a chat agent that has no exposed API said they can't use Cekura despite a genuine need, and asked whether testing chat agents directly through the UI is planned.
A commenter raised a concern with using agents to verify agents: the verifying agent may observe something a human would immediately find off-putting and obviously wrong, yet raise no flags.
A commenter praised Cekura's mock tool platform. They said testing agents against real APIs is a nightmare because of flakiness, burned rate limits, and failures that can't be reproduced.

A user described a support agent that called the 'refund order' tool when users only wanted to check order status. The tool worked; the LLM just picked the wrong one. They questioned whether Cekura's mock platform catches wrong tool selection, not only correct tool output.

Supporting full-session over turn-by-turn evaluation, a user said each turn of a verification flow looked fine in LangSmith (asked for name, asked for phone, processed request). But the agent never verified that the phone number matched the account, so the overall flow was broken.

A commenter called full-session evaluation the right call, saying teams often don't realize a failure happened in turn 2 until they've spent hours blaming the model. They asked whether simulation failures can be correlated back to real production sessions or whether that is still manual.
